reason: E3 directly supports the amorphization and nanobridge formation premise. E2 supports the grain boundary segregation premise and its link to ductility loss, though it focuses on a dual-phase strategy to mitigate it. However, no cited evidence supports the claimed competition mechanism governed by temperature/strain rate, nor the specific thresholds or the direct trade-off between the two mechanisms in a single-phase alloy.
premises: Deformation-induced crystalline-to-amorphous transformation occurs at crack tips in HEAs, forming nanoscale amorphous bridges that dissipate energy and resist crack propagation.
Grain boundary segregation of embrittling elements (e.g., Cr, Ni) reduces intergranular cohesion and leads to ductility loss in HEAs.
The competition between amorphization and segregation is governed by atomic mobility: low temperature/high strain rate favors amorphization, high temperature/low strain rate favors segregation.
The proposed mechanisms apply to single-phase, fine-grained HEAs like CrMnFeCoNi.
